findings.evidence: Async methods GetDirectorsAsync() (line 23), GetMoviesAsync() (line 31), GetMoviesByDirectorIdAsync() (line 39), and DeleteMovieAsync() (line 47) do not accept or forward a CancellationToken parameter. Each method calls _httpClient.GetAsync() or DeleteAsync(), both of which accept optional CancellationToken parameters, but no token is passed.
findings.fix_applied: All four methods now accept CancellationToken cancellationToken = default and pass it to _httpClient.GetAsync(..., cancellationToken), _httpClient.DeleteAsync(..., cancellationToken), and response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(cancellationToken).
findings.why_it_matters: CancellationToken propagation enables callers to cancel long-running HTTP operations and promptly free resources. Without token forwarding, HTTP requests initiated by consumers cannot be cancelled, risking hanging requests and resource exhaustion during application shutdown or timeout scenarios.
findings.required_action: Add CancellationToken parameter (with default value) to all four async method signatures and pass it through to the HttpClient calls. Example: `public async Task<List<DirectorResponse>> GetDirectorsAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)` followed by `await _httpClient.GetAsync($"{_baseUrl}/api/Directors/GetDirectors", cancellationToken);`

findings.evidence: HttpResponseMessage instances returned by GetAsync() (lines 25, 33, 41) and DeleteAsync() (line 49) are not wrapped in using statements or otherwise disposed deterministically. Each method obtains a response object, calls EnsureSuccessStatusCode(), reads the content, and returns without disposing.
findings.fix_applied: All four methods now use 'using var response = await ...' instead of bare 'var response = await ...' to ensure deterministic disposal of HttpResponseMessage.
findings.why_it_matters: HttpResponseMessage implements IDisposable and holds references to underlying HTTP content streams. Without explicit disposal, these resources remain allocated until garbage collection occurs, increasing memory pressure and delaying network resource reclamation under high load.
findings.required_action: Wrap each HttpResponseMessage in a using statement to ensure deterministic disposal. Example: `using (var response = await _httpClient.GetAsync(...)) { response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode(); var json = await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(); return JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(json, JsonOptions) ?? new(); }`
